notes: Five tier-0 ui-specs, refining the draft placeholders the tutorial-agent filed under the same ids in pipeline/proposals/tutorial-agent.json (see pipeline/gates/tutorial-review.md for the findings). Each spec below is implementation-ready: exact file, element, literal strings, classes, and CSS. No sfx items this cycle: all five are copy, data-plumbing, disabled-state, or event-wiring fixes with no new interaction beat to sonify; the existing generic UI press sound and win/lose stinger already cover every control touched. No music-brief. No art orders: no new chrome, no new icon, nothing outside the existing kp-teach/kp-result/kp-upg/kp-ability idiom. Item 5 (touch-safe-tooltips) is the one genuinely new piece of UI infrastructure in this batch (a long-press detector plus an inline popover); it is written to be reusable so any future touch-safe tip need reuses components/game/tap-tip.tsx rather than inventing a second mechanism. This file replaces the prior cycle's ux-agent.json (brief story-retune-1), whose items have already shipped per the repo's git history.

items.spec: screens.tsx, UpgradeScreen, the div.kp-patchrow.kp-cellrow block (currently lines 512-540). Only one line changes: the kp-rail-dim span that currently reads `PATCH CELLS {run.patchCells}/{PATCH_CELL_MAX}` becomes `PATCH CELLS {run.patchCells}/{PATCH_CELL_MAX} - {run.credits} cr`, mirroring exactly how the NIGHT PATCH row directly above it already reads `STRAIN {run.strain}/100 - {run.credits} cr - rest restored +{DAY_REST_REGEN}` (screens.tsx:508-510). Nothing else in the row moves: the button text, its disabled condition, the pip strip, and the trailing 'One slag block becomes a live cross junction. Single use.' span are all unchanged. The row's existing flex layout (`.kp-patchrow { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; }`) already has room for the extra clause without wrapping at normal window widths, so no CSS change is needed either.
acceptance: the kp-cellrow's PATCH CELLS span reads '{n}/{PATCH_CELL_MAX} - {credits} cr' on every render, matching the NIGHT PATCH row's price-plus-balance convention
the NIGHT PATCH row above it (screens.tsx:496-511) is untouched
the row's layout, button label, pip strip, and disabled state are unchanged when patch cells are already at PATCH_CELL_MAX or credits are below PATCH_CELL_COST

items.spec: shop-os.tsx:542, inside the ABANDON button's onClick. Replace the literal string passed to window.confirm from "Abandon this run? Unlocked routines are kept." to: "Abandon this run? This ends it exactly like a loss: kit, credits, and patch cells all reset for the next attempt." No other code changes: still a native window.confirm, still gating the same dispatch({ type: "endRunAck" }) on confirm only. The new string names nothing that persists and states the actual effect, framed against the loss overlay the player has already seen (duel.tsx:684-686, "Its flood got there first. Neural Strain zeroes. The run is over."), instead of the old string's false 'kept' claim.
acceptance: the confirm string makes no claim that kit tiers, program configs, augments, credits, or patch cells persist
the confirm string states plainly that the run ends or resets, in terms consistent with the strain-zero loss overlay
no em or en dash appears anywhere in the string
the control remains a native window.confirm gating the existing endRunAck dispatch, unchanged

items.spec: screens.tsx, UpgradeScreen's '+1 RAM / TURN' button (currently lines 485-491). Import MAX_RAM alongside the run-reducer constants already imported at the top of the file (DAY_REST_REGEN, GameState, PATCH_CELL_COST, PATCH_CELL_MAX, PATCH_COST, PATCH_HEAL, RunAction). Give the button the same disable-plus-relabel treatment tierBtn already gives the other three upgrade buttons (screens.tsx:451-468). Replace: ``` ``` with: ``` ``` No CSS change: .kp-upg carries no :disabled rule today, so the three tierBtn buttons rely on nothing but the bare disabled attribute plus their own label swap for a maxed cap, no extra dimming. Matching that exactly is the real parity target here, not adding a treatment tierBtn itself lacks. Flagging one pre-existing papercut out of scope for this item: none of the four .kp-upg buttons suppress their :hover border glow when disabled (`.kp-upg:hover` has no `:not(:disabled)` guard, unlike `.kp-job:hover:not(:disabled)` and `.kp-mode:hover:not(:disabled)` elsewhere in the file), so a maxed button of any of the four still glows on hover as if live. Shared by all four, not introduced by this fix, not proposing a change to it here.
acceptance: the RAM upgrade button is disabled and reads RAM MAXED once run.ramPerTurn is 9, in parallel with a tierBtn at tier 3
clicking it at the cap dispatches nothing, since a disabled button does not fire onClick
below the cap, the button's label, detail text, and click behavior are unchanged from today
MAX_RAM is imported from run-reducer.ts rather than redeclared or hardcoded
a chip caused only by over-par rotations shows exactly one breakdown line, 2 strain per rotation over par, summing to the same total shown today

a chip that includes trap or turn-cap contributions names them as separate lines with numbers matching duel-actions.ts's formula exactly (2 per rotation over par, 4 per trap sprung, +10 flat on a cap win)
when the raw sum of contributions exceeds 40, an extra capped line appears and the summary total still reads the true, already-capped value
a zero chip renders no breakdown list at all and the summary still reads clean
overRotations and trapsFired cross unchanged in value from finish() through duelFinished into RunState.lastResult
every one of the seven named title sites shows its tip text in an on-screen popover after a touch press-and-hold of about 400ms, with zero change to mouse hover behavior
holding a SCAN, ATTACK, or DEFEND ability button on a touch device opens kp-ability-info for that program without casting it; releasing before the hold threshold still casts, exactly as today
while a touch-opened tip or the ability panel is open, a second tap on the same control, or a tap anywhere else, closes it without also triggering that control's primary action
a long press never opens the native mobile text-selection or context-menu callout on any wrapped control
a long press on the THREAT pips inside a job card does not also select that job
mouse and keyboard users see no behavior change at all: title tooltips on hover, ability info on mouseenter/mouseleave/focus/blur, exactly as before
